summary.text: The Jansky Very Large Array is a centimeter-wavelength radio astronomy observatory in the southwestern United States, built in the 1970s.
It has 28 radio telescopes, each 25 meters across, set in a Y-shaped array and working together as an interferometer.
The dishes sit on railroad tracks and can be moved, so the array acts as a single antenna with a variable diameter.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The Plains of San Agustin in central New Mexico

facts.label: Arm length
facts.value: Each of its three arms measures 21 kilometers

facts.label: Configuration cycle
facts.value: Every 16 months it cycles through its configurations

items.prompt: Astronomers want to change how the array balances fine detail against sensitivity to dim, spread-out glow. How can they do it?

options.label: Swap every dish for a much larger one
Slide the dishes along the tracks to resize the array
Wait until the Sun moves across the sky
Switch some of the dishes off for good

items.explain: The antennas ride on double parallel railroad tracks so the radius and density of the array can be adjusted to balance angular resolution and surface brightness sensitivity.

items.prompt: One team wants to study hydrogen gas in the Milky Way, and another wants to study pulsars. Can the same observatory serve both?

options.label: Only if it is rebuilt between projects
No, since it is built for planets only
No, since it can study one object type only
Yes, since it is a multi-purpose instrument

items.explain: The VLA was designed to investigate many kinds of objects, from pulsars and quasars to the hydrogen gas in the Milky Way.

items.prompt: The original array was built in the 1970s. What did its decade-long upgrade change?

options.label: New electronics boosted its sensitivity and range
It moved the whole array to a new state
It took out the railroad tracks entirely
It turned the array into an optical telescope

items.explain: The upgrade swapped the 1970s-era electronics for state-of-the-art equipment and expanded the array's technical capacities.

items.prompt: A space agency needs a huge receiver to catch the weak radio signals of a probe flying past Neptune. What did the VLA do in a case like this?

options.label: It transmitted commands to the probe
It received the radio communications from Voyager 2
It photographed the planet in visible light
It steered the probe with its dishes

items.explain: The VLA was used to receive radio communications from the Voyager 2 spacecraft as it flew by Neptune.

items.prompt: Which finding did astronomers using the array make at the center of the Milky Way?

options.label: A ring of planets around the central star
A new moon orbiting the black hole
Magnetic filaments and complex gas motions
A hidden cluster of visible stars

items.explain: VLA astronomers discovered magnetic filaments and traced complex gas motions at the Milky Way's center.

items.prompt: The array has 28 dishes, but only 27 are in use at a given time. Why?

options.label: One is always rotating through maintenance
One is pointed at the ground
One is too heavy to move
One belongs to another observatory

items.explain: 27 are operational while one is always rotating through maintenance, so there is one spare.
